subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@auroraai.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@auroraai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - follow-up & next steps

Hi Samir/Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Aurora AI infra & product team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap (high level):
- Aurora goal: consistent low-latency inference for real-time chat (p99 < 300ms), peak concurrent sessions ~450, average sequence length ~512 tokens.
- Primary models: 70B class chat models (quantized variants), some smaller embedding workloads for search.
- Key concerns: capacity guarantees during peak events, predictable cost, and enterprise compliance (VPC/KMS).

How Redwood differentiates vs hyperscalers (summary):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): predictable throughput and isolation vs ephemeral hyperscaler endpoints which can throttle during spikes.
- Capacity guarantees & SLOs: Dedicated comes with commit-backed throughput and optional burst capacity; hyperscalers typically offer best-effort autoscaling.
- Cost controls: batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles we tune per workload to lower per-token cost vs naive hyperscaler usage.
- Operational tooling: per-route dashboards, tracing, and rollback/rollout policies (canary/A-B) built into the platform.

Requested next tests (proposal):
1) Small POC: 48–72 hour perf run on a representative 70B quantized model with your sample payloads (we'll mirror QPS/seq len). Goal: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.
2) Spike test: a scheduled short test to validate burst capacity during a simulated flash (x3 baseline QPS).
3) Failover behavior: validate multi-region fallback if a primary pool is constrained.

What we need from Aurora to scope the POC:
- Typical/peak QPS and concurrency targets (you mentioned ~450 concurrent sessions — can you confirm peak queries/s?).
- Exact model binary (name/weights) or a close proxy we can run.
- Any compliance requirements (SOC2/DFARS/etc) for evidence in the POC.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-datasheet.pdf, redwood-sow-template.docx (SOW draft for Dedicated POC).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You confirm the targets above by EOD Tue 9/7.
- We get SE (Laura) access to your sample payloads and model descriptor.
- Kick off POC the week of 9/13 if timelines align.

I'll follow up with a short technical plan (Laura will share). Let me know if you want a pricing ballpark for a 3-month reserved commitment vs pay-as-you-go.

Thanks,
Markus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--

Date: 2026-09-07T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - follow-up & next steps

Markus — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline: 

> Typical/peak QPS and concurrency targets
We expect baseline QPS ~600 req/s during normal hours with average concurrency ~300. Peak (marketing pushes) could approach ~1800 req/s for short bursts (~15–30 mins), which is why capacity guarantees matter. The 450 concurrent sessions I mentioned was per-region; apologies for the confusion — total concurrency across regions is higher.

> Model
We plan to run a quantized 70B chat model (internal build based on open weights). We can provide a model descriptor and sample payloads — Priya will attach a dataset and a small inference manifest.

> Compliance
SOC2 is required; we also need audit logs and key management (KMS) integration.

As for procurement, finance will want a pricing comparison: 12‑month reserved vs on-demand. Can you provide a ballpark TCO for both (GPU-hours and estimated token costs) ahead of POC? We need that to justify reserved spend.

Happy to move forward with the POC week of 9/13.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Infrastructure | Aurora AI
samir.gupta@auroraai.com | +1 347-555-7788

Hi Samir/Priya — attaching the POC test plan and checklist. High-level summary below and a short technical checklist you can complete to accelerate access.

POC test plan (short):
- Duration: 48 hours core perf run + 1 scheduled spike window (20 minutes).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token cost estimate, KV/prefix cache hit rates.
- Scenarios: steady-state baseline (600 req/s), burst (1800 req/s), network failover simulation.

Technical checklist (what we need to run the POC):
- Model descriptor (weights path, tokenizer, quantization type) — Priya to share.
- Sample payloads: 1k typical chats and 200 spike synthetic requests.
- SSH/key access for our SE runner or OCI/AWS role in your lab environment (we can run from Redwood VPC if you prefer).
- Acceptance criteria: p99 <= 300ms for baseline; successful controlled spike to 1800 req/s with graceful degradation and defined cost envelope.

Compliance evidence we can provide for SOC2 scoped items: audit logs, KMS integration guide, retention settings, and diagrams. If you need a formal evidence package we have a SOC2 packet we can share under an NDA.

DocuSign: I also pushed a short SOW (redwood-sow-template.docx) to DocuSign for signature to speed procurement — link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123

If that looks good, Markus — once Priya drops the artifacts we can schedule an access window and lock the POC dates.

Thanks,
